This bail application is filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.991 of 2024 of Ernakulam Town South Police Station,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 354 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 r/w Sections 3(a), 4(1), 4(2), 6(1) and 51 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (as amended by the 2019 Amendment).
3.

sentences.text: According to the prosecution, the accused, who is a family friend of the victim, had during the period from May, 2022 till March, 2024 on several occasions committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim, who is a minor and thereby committed the offences alleged.
4. Heard Sri.Tom Jose, the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Smt.Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor.
The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the entire prosecution allegations are false and no such incident had ever occurred.
It was further submitted that complaint has been raised for the purpose of blackmailing the petitioner and extorting money from him.
According to the learned counsel, the victim has been making contradictory statements and therefore her version is not reliable.
The learned counsel further submitted that petitioner was arrested on 06.11.2024 and therefore further detention ought to be avoided.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand vehemently opposed the application and submitted that considering the nature of allegations, petitioner ought not to be released on bail.

It was also submitted that the investigation has already been completed and the final report has also been filed and hence if petitioner is released on bail, there is every chance of him influencing the Ganesh Chandra Patra vs State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126482314/
2 witnesses.

sentences.text: 7. While considering the rival contentions, this Court called for the case diary, primarily to verify the medical report of the victim, since petitioner asserted that it was a false case.
Initially, the victim refused to undergo medical examination stating that she has fears about pain during examination.
Subsequently, on another day she was medically examined.

In the absence BAIL APPL. NO. 6897 OF 2025 2025:KER:39190 of any medical evidence to assume that she was subjected to penetrative sexual assault, the contention of the petitioner regarding false allegation cannot be brushed aside.
8. Apart from the above, the statement of the victim also indicates some contradictions though that they may not be relevant at this juncture or be treated as significant.

However, considering the fact that in the absence of any noting in the medical certificate regarding tearing of the hymen and considering the period of detention already undergone by the petitioner from 06.11.2024, I am of the view that continued detention is not necessary.

9. In the result, this application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(a) Petitioner shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the court having jurisdiction.
(b) Petitioner shall co-
operate with the trial of the case.
(c) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he attempt to tamper with the evidence.
(d) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
(e) Petitioner shall not leave the country without the permission of the jurisdictional Court.
(f). Petitioner shall not enter into the limits of Ernakulam Town South Police Station until conclusion of the trial.
BAIL APPL. NO. 6897 OF 2025 2025:KER:39190

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.

Sd/-
